activities.title: A Ventana sales order is allocated from a Taylor warehouse and nothing refuses it
activities.trigger: A Ventana deal needs a part that only Main Distribution Center holds, and Main belongs to Taylor.
activities.narrative: The Sales Order genuinely carries an operating company — the commercial axis lands it there at creation. The warehouse genuinely belongs to an operating company too. Nothing compares them. The allocation command contains no reference to `operatingCompanyId` at all, and the commercial-company module states in its own source that the field is optional everywhere, that there is no enforcement, and that none may be added until the census gate passes. So the seam does not fail loudly: it succeeds, and the record of which company's stock satisfied which company's order is simply never made.

Company on the warehouse: config/ownership/operating-company-roots.sandbox.json (wh-main -> taylor, wh-north -> ventana), assignment module functions/src/ownership/warehouseRootCompanyAssignment.ts. Allocation: functions/src/fulfillment/allocateSalesOrder.ts:96, whose eligible pool is 'status==ACTIVE warehouses' (:119) with NO company predicate — grep for `operatingCompanyId` across that file returns zero matches. The no-enforcement statement is functions/src/ownership/commercialCompanyScope.ts:26-29.
activities.owner_question: May a Sales Order booked to Ventana be fulfilled from a Taylor warehouse? Today the allocation command does not look at the operating company at all (allocateSalesOrder.ts has no reference to it), and commercialCompanyScope.ts:26-29 states that no enforcement may be added until the census gate passes. If the answer is 'yes, and it creates an intercompany obligation', that obligation has nowhere to be recorded — FIN-BLOCK-004 forbids an intercompany record type until the treatment is ruled.

activities.title: A salesperson holds the capability to create a customer and Firestore refuses the write
activities.trigger: A salesperson tries to add a prospect from the accounts list.
activities.narrative: Two authorities give two answers and the one that wins is the older one. The capability model says the Salesperson role holds `customer.record.create`, and it is one of only 37 capabilities that resolve ALLOW in production. The write path, however, is a client-direct Firestore write governed by a Rules helper that reads a single legacy string field on the user document and admits only 'admin' or 'dispatcher'. A salesperson whose user record does not carry one of those two strings is denied, capability or not. The repository knows: it maintains a machine-checked corpus of every remaining legacy call site precisely so this can be retired provably.

Rules side: `accounts` create gated on `isAdminOrDispatcher()` firestore.rules:1332-1334, that helper defined :22-24 reading `userRole()` :18-20 which is `users/{uid}.role` — a single legacy string, not the governed model. Write path is client-direct: field-ops-app-vite/src/domain/accounts.js:78. Corpus: functions/src/access/legacyAuthorizationSurface.ts:52-74 measures 44 enforced legacy call sites across 22 collections (was 47; the shrink is recorded :63-74), with `accounts` carrying 3 `isAdminOrDispatcher` and 2 `isAdmin` sites (:104-105); CI re-parses the real rules file to enforce the count (functions/test/legacyAuthorizationSurface.test.mjs).

output: customer.record.update | prodAllow = officeManager, salesManager, salesperson, generalManager, owner, admin, dispatcher
Rules `isAdminOrDispatcher()` admits exactly two legacy role strings: "admin" and "dispatcher".
execution.note: The capability resolution is executed; the Rules denial is read from the deployed ruleset, not executed against an emulator. Five of the seven capability holders (officeManager, salesManager, salesperson, generalManager, owner) are not admitted by the Rules helper.

activities.owner_question: Five roles hold `customer.record.update` in the capability model and are refused by the Firestore Rules that actually govern the write (officeManager, salesManager, salesperson, generalManager, owner). Which is the intended authority for customer master data, and should the trusted server-side writer named in firestore.rules:1329-1331 be built before more roles are granted capabilities they cannot exercise?

activities.title: A part is renamed in the catalog after it is quoted and before the work order completes
activities.trigger: A catalog administrator corrects an internal part number while an order is in fulfilment.
activities.narrative: The part number is captured twice at two different moments and compared later. When the service work order is raised, the parts plan is seeded with a SKU resolved from Part Master at that instant and deliberately never fabricated from the part id. When the technician completes, the fulfilment write-back derives the PART lines' quantities by matching that snapshot's SKU against the sales order line reference. Change the canonical internal part number in between and the two captures no longer describe the same string. The catalog capabilities that permit the rename are among the few live in production; the write-back that depends on the old value is not.

Matching at completion: functions/src/salesOrder/salesOrderFulfillmentWriteBack.ts:63-75 (`keyOf(kind, ref)` :63-64, fallback match by `(ref,kind)` :75) — and note the header :7-15 records that matching is now PRIMARILY by a stable `lineId` with `(ref,kind)` only as a legacy fallback, which is a change beyond what docs/design/p1-fulfillment-billing-spine-spec.md:29 specifies. Rename authority: `inventory.catalog.manage` functions/src/access/permissionCatalog.ts:1071 (ACTIVE, resolves ALLOW in production) via `updatePart` functions/src/index.ts:351.
activities.owner_question: Nothing prevents a Part's internal part number being changed while a Sales Order referencing it is in fulfilment. Should `inventory.catalog.manage` refuse a rename on a part with open commitments, or should the fulfilment write-back key on the immutable part id rather than the mutable SKU?

activities.title: Cash from one customer settles a related customer's invoice
activities.trigger: A franchise parent pays for three of its franchisees' invoices with one cheque.
activities.narrative: There is no customer hierarchy, so the two parties are unrelated records as far as EOS is concerned. The payment command requires the receipt to be fully applied to invoices on receipt — unapplied cash is explicitly unsupported — and nothing models one account paying another's debt. The practical effect is that the most common real-world payment pattern in a franchise business has no representation: either the cheque is recorded against the wrong customer, or it is not recorded at all.
activities.authority_path: Payment command functions/src/finance/paymentCallables.ts:62 over functions/src/finance/paymentCommands.ts; over-application rejected :129-130 ('unapplied balances are not yet supported'), `unappliedMinor` always 0 :150. No customer hierarchy exists: no parent/child column on `CREATE TABLE accounts` functions/migrations/1758758400000_crm-account-contact-location.sql:170-191, nothing in field-ops-app-vite/src/metadata/definitions/account.js:67; the topic is assessed only at docs/assessments/customer-hierarchy.md.
activities.owner_question: How should a payment from a parent company covering several franchisees' invoices be recorded? EOS has no customer hierarchy and `applyPayment` binds a receipt to invoices on one account. Recording it against the payer misstates that account's AR; recording it against each franchisee misstates who paid.

activities.title: An employee is disabled mid-work-order while still the assigned technician
activities.trigger: An employee walks off site and HR asks for access to be cut the same afternoon.
activities.narrative: Disabling access and reassigning work are different acts governed by different authorities, and only the first has a command. Setting user status is an active capability held by administrators and owners; nothing in that path examines whether the person is the assigned technician on open work. The work order keeps pointing at a principal who can no longer authenticate, and the reassignment is a separate scheduling act somebody has to remember to perform.

activities.owner_question: Disabling a principal does not check whether they are the assigned technician on open work orders, and nothing reassigns that work. Should `setUserStatus` refuse, warn, or queue an exception when the subject holds open assignments?

activities.title: A report is run by a user whose role grant changed between the schedule and the execution
activities.trigger: A report is saved on Monday by a manager whose role is narrowed on Wednesday, and run on Friday.
activities.narrative: This seam is closed, and closed well — it is worth recording as the counter-example. A saved definition confers no data access. Every run reads the runner's access version and active assignments fresh from the database, then re-resolves the object capability, every field capability and every relationship traversal against that state. Memoization is scoped to the single call and nothing is cached across calls. The report shows the runner what the runner may see on Friday, not what the author could see on Monday.

Saved-definition header functions/src/reporting/savedDefinitionCommands.ts:22-29 and :32-35.

activities.title: An opportunity's operating company is corrected after invoices have already issued against it
activities.trigger: A deal was booked to Taylor and should have been Ventana; two invoices have shipped.
activities.narrative: The system deliberately refuses to make the correction propagate. The company is copied downstream at creation, not followed, so correcting the Opportunity cannot silently rewrite the company on invoices already issued against it — historical company responsibility stays historical, exactly as ownership does. That is the right behaviour and it leaves the business with an unrepresentable state: two records that disagree about which company conducted the same deal, and no reclassification act to record why.
activities.authority_path: functions/src/ownership/commercialCompanyScope.ts:21-24 ('COPIED, NOT FOLLOWED ... correcting an Opportunity cannot silently rewrite the company on invoices that were already issued against it'). Writers functions/src/opportunity/opportunityCommands.ts:175, functions/src/salesAgreement/salesAgreementCommands.ts:304, functions/src/salesOrder/salesOrderCommands.ts:287. No void path to reverse the invoices: functions/migrations/1758931200000_invoice-authority.sql:94-99.
activities.owner_question: When a deal was booked to the wrong operating company and invoices have issued, what is the correcting act? The company is deliberately immutable downstream, invoices cannot be voided, and there is no intercompany reclassification record (FIN-BLOCK-004).

activities.title: A saved report survives its author's departure and keeps naming them as owner
activities.trigger: A manager leaves; their saved reports remain.
activities.narrative: The reports keep working for anyone else who can run them, because authorization is the runner's. What cannot happen is cleanup: the report author role can create, rename and duplicate definitions but cannot delete them, and delete is held only by administrators and owners. So the person best placed to tidy a departed colleague's reports is the one role that cannot.

activities.title: An account owner is removed while open opportunities inherit from them
activities.trigger: A salesperson leaves and their accounts are un-assigned before the replacement starts.
activities.narrative: Removing the owner does not disturb the opportunities that already exist — the matrix is explicit that a downstream record takes ownership at creation and keeps it. activities.title: Equipment is sold between two customers and the installed-base record cannot follow it
activities.trigger: One franchisee sells a used ice machine to another operator EOS also services.
activities.narrative: The Rules restrict an equipment update to a key set that deliberately excludes the account and the location, so the record cannot be reparented from the client. There is no server-side reparent command either, so this is not a client restriction with a governed alternative — it is an absence. The machine physically moves and the record cannot.

activities.title: An administrator reads that a capability is granted to nobody and believes it
activities.trigger: Reviewing the exports file to decide what is safe to activate.
activities.narrative: Five comments in the functions index and one in the Rules file assert that certain capabilities are granted to nobody. All are false, because the administrator role is constructed as its curated list plus every remaining catalog id. The consequence is not academic: someone deciding whether to flip an activation flag would conclude that activation alone changes nothing, when in fact it immediately grants the capability to every administrator and owner in the system.
